title: Secure Release Gate for Model Rollouts: RBAC, Audit, and Data Residency Checklist
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This document defines the Secure Release Gate used by product, platform, and security teams to approve model rollouts (hosted, dedicated, and private) where RBAC, audit logging, and data residency obligations intersect. The gate ties technical checks, evidence artifacts, and incident hooks into a single, repeatable approval workflow that must be completed before a model is promoted to production traffic.

Scope

- Applies to any model or model variant (quantized or full-precision) being promoted to a production-serving tier.
- Covers checks for: RBAC entitlements, audit logging completeness, data residency mapping, secure SDLC verification, incident-response readiness, and compliance evidence packaging.
- Excludes client-side SDK updates that do not change server-side inference logic (see related release checklist).

Goals

1. Ensure least-privilege access to model control and invocation endpoints.
2. Guarantee sufficient telemetry and immutable audit trails for regulatory and forensic needs.
3. Verify that data residency boundaries are respected by inference path and logs.
4. Provide a clear incident escalation path and packaged evidence to accelerate investigations.

Gate Owner and Decision Authority

- Gate steward: Security Engineering (primary): @security-release-gate.
- Final approval: Combined sign-off from Product Owner and Security Lead.
- Supporting teams: Serving Runtime, SRE, Platform, Compliance.

Gate Criteria (quick checklist)

1) RBAC Entitlement Review (MUST)
   - All service and user principals touching the model are documented.
   - Role bindings follow attribute-based rules: environment, team, and purpose.
   - No direct granting of privileged roles (model-admin/model-maintainer) to long-lived human accounts.
   - Just-in-time (JIT) activation configured for emergency maintenance where applicable.

2) Audit Logging & Telemetry (MUST)
   - Request-level logs: every model invocation records request_id, caller_principal, model_id, input_hash (if storing), timestamp, and region.
   - Immutable audit sink enabled (WORM/immutable S3 or equivalent) for retention period required by tenancy.
   - Trace sampling set to 100% for canary traffic window (see rollout policy).

3) Data Residency Manifest (MUST)
   - Inference path diagram with all ingress/egress hops and regions.
   - Classification of input, output, and logs (PII / pseudonymous / non-sensitive).
   - Storage & retention targets per artifact type (see table below).

4) Secure SDLC Gates (MUST)
   - Model artifact provenance verified (checksum + signed provenance file).
   - Static analysis / dependency checks run for model-serving container.
   - Vulnerability scan pass for runtime image (no critical/high unmitigated).

5) Incident Response Hooks (MUST)
   - Incident runbook for this model registered and linked.
   - Ownership roster and on-call contacts included.
   - Automated evidence packaging enabled on incident trigger.

6) Compliance Evidence Packaging (MUST)
   - Evidence manifest prepared containing: RBAC snapshot, audit-log snapshot window, deployment artifact checksums, data residency diagram, and change approvals.

Detailed Pre-Release Checklist (step-by-step)

1. Preflight (authoring team)
   a. Create Release Request in the Release Tracker and attach this Gate checklist.
   b. Provide model metadata: model_id, version, base_model, quantization_profile, expected token patterns.
   c. Attach provenance file (signed) and packaging manifest.

2. RBAC Entitlement Validation (Platform)
   - Run the entitlement-export tool and attach resulting CSV.
   - Verify no human account has persistent model-admin role.
   - If service-accounts require expanded privileges, attach JIRA for justification with TTL (max 72 hours).

3. Audit & Logging Verification (SRE)
   - Confirm audit-forwarder configuration: fields forwarded, retention tier, encryption at rest.
   - Execute a synthetic invocation test that exercises canary route and verify log ingestion in immutable store.
   - Confirm log redaction rules applied for PII fields.

4. Data Residency Mapping (Compliance)
   - Provide a data flow ASCII/diagram showing region hops.
   - Map each artifact to residency requirement and retention policy.

5. Secure SDLC Checks (Build & Release)
   - Verify signed build artifact and container image digest.
   - Attach SBOM and vulnerability scan report.

6. Incident Readiness (Security)
   - Validate runbook is current and the on-call rotation is listed with current contacts.
   - Configure automated evidence snapshot: command and retention window.

Audit Evidence Manifest (table representation)

| Artifact | Required fields | Retention location | Retention period |
|---------|-----------------|--------------------|------------------|
| RBAC snapshot | timestamp, exporter, role bindings CSV | restricted-audit-bucket (eu-west-1) | 7 years |
| Invocation logs | request_id, caller, model_id, input_hash, region | immutable-s3/audit | 3 years (or as customer SLA) |
| Deployment artifact | image_digest, SBOM, provenance.sig | artifact-registry | 10 years |
| Data residency diagram | diagram.png, classification.csv | compliance-docs | indefinite (versioned) |

Note: retention periods should align with contractual/legal requirements; document deviations in the Exceptions section.

RBAC Entitlement Validation Steps (commands & expectations)

- Export current bindings: 
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://infra-api.internal/v1/rbac/export?scope=model:${MODEL_ID} | jq . > rbac-${MODEL_ID}-snapshot.json
- Expected checks:
  - No human account in model-admin role.
  - Service accounts must have least-privilege roles and TTL-tagged credentials where possible.

Audit Logging Health Checks

1. Synthetic trace: run the canary invocation test against canary route for 1 hour, collect traces and confirm ingestion.
2. Verify encryption: KMS key id present and rotated in last 90 days.
3. Confirm immutability flag: bucket/object store has immutability (WORM) enabled for audit namespace.

Data Residency and Log Minimization Guidance

- Prefer pseudonymization at the edge when input contains PII; send only hashed identifiers and include salt provenance in evidence manifest.
- Logs that cannot be pseudonymized must be routed to region-specific immutable stores.
- When rolling out cross-region models, include a per-tenant residency binding file that maps tenant_id -> allowed_regions.

Incident Response Hooks (how the gate integrates)

- Trigger points that auto-escalate to Security Incident Response (SIR):
  1) Unauthorized privileged access to model control plane.
  2) Sudden spike in model invocations from single principal (> 1k RPS sustained for 5 minutes outside baseline).
  3) Evidence of data exfiltration (large log downloads or cross-region transfers violating tenant binding).

- On trigger, automated playbook will run:
  a. Freeze model rollout traffic.
  b. Snapshot RBAC, last 30 minutes of invocation logs, deployment metadata, and system traces.
  c. Push evidence package to incident bucket and notify SIR and on-call.

Evidence Packaging Format (required files)

- evidence-manifest.json (fields: incident_id, collected_at, artifacts list)
- rbac-snapshot.json
- invocation-logs-<window>.ndjson.gz
- image-digest.txt
- provenance.sig
- residency-mapping.csv

Exception & Risk Handling

- Any deviation from the gate MUST be recorded as a formal exception using the Exception Request template. Exception requests require: business justification, compensating controls, owner, TTL, and approver (Security Lead).
- Short-lived exceptions (<=72 hours) may be approved by Security Lead + Product Manager; longer exceptions require cross-functional review and treasury notification if cost increases are expected.

Operational SLAs & Metrics to Monitor

- Gate processing SLA: 48 business hours for standard release requests, 8 business hours for emergency releases (with JIT justification).
- SLOs to track: percentage of releases with complete evidence on first submission (target: 95%), average time to diagnose an access incident using packaged evidence (target: <4 hours), number of RBAC violations detected post-rollout (target: 0).

Appendix: Sample evidence-manifest.json (example)

{
  "incident_id": "INC-2026-0123",
  "collected_at": "2026-07-10T14:03:00Z",
  "artifacts": [
    "rbac-snapshot.json",
    "invocation-logs-2026-07-10-13-30-14-03.ndjson.gz",
    "image-digest.txt",
    "provenance.sig",
    "residency-mapping.csv"
  ]
}
